encounters.weakness: Burnt Ember Shard (pickup from previous encounter) - reduces damage by 30% when used against this enemy. Can be thrown at the enemy to trigger the weakness.
Ashen Flame Staff — when the player attacks with their weapon while the enemy is on fire, it deals 50% extra damage. The staff must be used in a melee attack to trigger the weakness.

Emberheart Core (pickup from previous encounter) — when the player uses the Emberheart Core at the start of the battle, the boss takes 30% damage for 20 seconds. The core must be used during the first turn to activate. Without it, the boss gains a 'Fire Resilience' buff that reduces all fire damage by 40%.
Player's weapon (Flute of the Wind Reeds)
Glowing Moss Token (must be used during combat)
Whistle of the Wind (must be activated during combat)

Holy Blade of Saint Vael (player weapon) - 30% damage reduction and 25% healing on hit. If blade is broken, weakness lost and damage increases by 40%. Damage increases by 10% each time the player fails to use the weapon in combat.

Charged Holy Ember (pickup from previous encounter) - When used, deals 50% extra damage and causes a 10-second 'Divine Drain' where enemy gains 30 HP per second until the effect ends. If Ember is not used, enemy gains 25% resistance to Holy and Divine Damage, and consumes player's divine power at 10% per second.

Charged Holy Ember (pickup from previous encounter) - Using it during battle deals 75% more damage and forces the enemy to enter 'Shadow Resonance' for 10 seconds, where it gains 50% more damage and is immune to healing. If not used, the enemy gains 40% resistance to Holy Damage, and mimics the player's actions—stealing divine aura and placing a temporary 'Soul Anchor' that drains player health over time (2 HP per second). If player loses divine aura, the temple collapses and boss appears immediately.

The Reality Shard (player weapon) is the only thing that can shatter the Fumes' illusions. If the illusionist fails to use it, the Fumes will manifest as a solid, breathing entity, and their damage increases by 30% per second. They cannot be hurt by direct physical attacks — only by truth-based illusions that show them as they truly are (e.g., a mirror reflecting their own face in pain).

The Flicker Shard (a pickup from Encounter 1) must be used during the enemy's first 10 seconds of attack. If used, the enemy's reflection will flicker into a state of self-annihilation, and it will lose 30% of its health immediately. However, if the Flicker Shard is not used, the mirror begins to *learn* the illusionist's patterns. After 5 seconds, it emits a pulse of reality distortion that causes all illusions to become fixed, and all illusions fail. The enemy then becomes immune to illusions and gains 20% damage resistance and 30% increased attack speed. This creates a brutal loop where every illusion attempt is punished.

The Void Lens (pickup from Encounter 2) must be used within 3 seconds of the enemy spawning. If used, the enemy becomes vulnerable to all illusions and its defense drops by 50%. However, if the Void Lens is not used, the enemy begins to *recreate* the first enemy (Whispering Fumes), but with 40% increased health and 25% faster attack speed. It then begins to reflect the illusionist's own spells back at them, with a 10-second delay, causing a feedback loop where every illusion fails and damages the player. After 20 seconds, the enemy splits into two: one mirror, one physical form. This creates an infinite loop of failed illusions and real attacks. The only way to end it is to use the Void Lens.

The Luminous Willow Staff deals 1.5x damage to Moss Sprites due to its gentle, radiant energy that resonates with the forest's living mosses. The staff's glow causes the sprite to tremble and stutter in attack.

The Moss Shard enhances the player's staff's radiant pulse. When the player uses the shard while attacking, the Willow Wisp takes 30% more damage. Its movements become sluggish when exposed to the combined energy of the staff and shard.

The Sentinel is vulnerable to the Whispering Leaf when its core resonance is disrupted. The leaf causes it to emit a faint, discordant sound — which activates a defensive pattern that leaves it momentarily exposed. The player can use the Whispering Leaf to trigger a 3-second vulnerability window where the Sentinel's health drops 30% per second for 3 seconds. This is the only weakness the player can use to defeat it.
Crimson Fang in Rage Mode (player weapon state, requires rage swing to trigger weakness)
Rage Shard (must be thrown at wraith to shatter — if not thrown, wraiths transform into Fury Wraith Twin, immune to weapon damage)
Core Shard (must be used as a projectile — only works if it was collected from first fight)
Soul Reaver (bone-etched blade) - deals 30% extra damage to bone-etched weapons. No elemental damage resistance.
Shard of the First Bone - reduces enemy's necromantic magic by 50% when held in hand during combat. Only active if the shard is equipped at the start of battle.

Whispering Bone Fragment - when activated, reduces Vaelthar's necrotic regeneration by 75%. The fragment must be held in hand during the final battle to trigger its effect. Without it, the player cannot win the fight.

The Longbow - Ironwood fires a single shot that knocks the wraith into a defensive crouch, reducing its evasion by 40%. It cannot move or attack while crouched for 3 seconds. The shot is silent, and the wraith's shadow is visible in the dust for 3 seconds. If the player misses, it emits a low hum and gains 20% more evasion for 10 seconds. It is vulnerable to arrows during crouch state only. This is the only weakness in its existence.

The Silt-Soaked Arrow Tip can be used to detonate a secondary charge in a specific arc. When the tip is used on Ashfang while it is in mid-leap (a state triggered by its movement), the player causes a localized ash explosion that reduces Ashfang's mobility by 50% and deals 30% extra damage to the upper body. The player must time this with the enemy's leap—only one such opportunity occurs per 15 seconds. If the player fails to hit during the leap, Ashfang enters a 'Feral Phase' where it gains 35% damage resistance and can only be attacked with a melee weapon (which the player has none).

The Vexed One is only vulnerable to the Frost-Drift Resonance Shard when it is in a state of 'Echo-Scream'—a phase it enters when it detects the player's presence through sound. This state occurs every 45 seconds. During this state, it is completely still and cannot attack. The player can use the Frost-Drift Resonance Shard to trigger a 'Freeze-Release' that causes the Vexed One to shatter its own armor and reveal its core. This reveals a single, pulsing core that is vulnerable to the Silt-Soaked Arrow Tip—only one such core exists, and it can be struck only once. If the player does not hit the core during the Echo-Scream, the Vexed One enters a 'Cacophony' state where it emits sound waves that reduce all player movement and damage by 30% for 10 seconds, and all enemies in range (even if not present) gain 10% evasion. This state cannot be broken without the shard or the arrow tip.
Quantum Pulse Rifle (charged pulse burst) — when fired at 90% charge, causes localized EMP surge that disrupts their corrosion field and briefly disables their movement system for 2 seconds.

Magnetic Clamp (used on power node) — when the player attaches the clamp to a live node, a 120-volt pulse is induced, causing a feedback surge that weakens the Synth by 40% and stuns it for 3 seconds. Requires exact positioning to succeed.

Circuit Resonance Core (must be activated during the 'Feedback Pulse' phase). When the player uses the Resonance Core at exactly 100% charge during the final 15 seconds of its phase, it emits a destructive resonance that disables the Overmind for 10 seconds and deals 100% damage. If not used, the Overmind activates self-replication and spawns 2 additional drones.

Chrono-Spike (player weapon) — when the player uses the Chrono-Spike in a *reverse time pulse*, it briefly freezes the droid's movements and triggers a feedback loop that shatters its internal time circuits. The attack must be timed to a specific phase of its movement cycle (shown by a fading red pulse).

Temporal Resonance Shard — if the player uses the shard *during the enemy's movement phase*, it emits a harmonic pulse that disrupts their internal time sync, causing them to loop backward through their own attack pattern. This reveals a hidden weak point where their next move is predictable. The enemy now moves in a 3-second loop that repeats once per 4 seconds (during which it is vulnerable).

Temporal Resonance Shard — the shard must be used in a *synchronized resonance pulse* during the boss's *time fracture phase* (which occurs every 20 seconds). This phase is marked by a fractured, jagged light pattern and a 3-second stutter in the environment. Using the shard here causes a *temporal collapse* in the boss's core, reducing its health by 25% and resetting one of its time loops. The boss cannot use its full attack during this phase. The shard must be *previously obtained* from the second encounter to be usable.

Charged Storm Staff (when fully charged during attack phase). If staff is uncharged, the drone gains immunity to all damage and emits a psychic pulse that causes player control drift (reduces precision by 30%).

Storm Fragment (must be thrown into its core during the 'mind-scream' phase). If not used, the Echo evolves into a faster, more aggressive form with 40% increased attack speed and 60% increased damage. If thrown, it causes a mental resonance burst that briefly freezes the Echo's movement (1.5 seconds).

Must use the Storm Fragment at precisely 30% health to trigger a 'Storm Resonance' effect. If used, it causes a 10-second surge of contained storm energy that damages the Leviathan by 600 HP and disables its environmental manipulation for 5 seconds. If used too late (after 40% health), it causes a 30% chance of player shock and failure to trigger. If not used, the Leviathan evolves into a 'Fractured Storm' form — with 150% health, 300% damage, and adaptive AI that mimics player attacks.
Luminal Core Injector (injection causes the Mimic to glitch and lose motion control for 3 seconds).
Stabilized Data Shard (when the player uses Echo Pulse, the Vulture is stunned and its vision is mirrored — it sees the player's own reflection and attacks itself, causing 50% damage to its health).

Resonant Frequency Crystal (the Symbiont is only vulnerable when the player uses 'Flicker Recall' to reveal a specific memory pattern — the memory of the first encounter. When this memory is triggered, the Symbiont's core destabilizes and takes 50% damage).
Nyx-9 Shadow Dagger (only when blade is fully plunged into darkness; the dagger's shadow-siphon effect amplifies damage when used in pitch-black zones).

Shard of Echoed Light (the enemy's shadow-forms are visible only during the shard's activation — when active, the Maw's true form is revealed as a floating, mechanical swarm of shadowed limbs. The player must strike it at full visibility to deal double damage).

Frayed Pulse Core (only when the Frayed Pulse Core is equipped AND the player is within 2 meters of a shadowed surface — e.g., a dark wall or floor — the Core-Skull emits a feedback pulse, revealing its true form as a fragmented consciousness of the station. The player must strike it in this state to deal 2x damage. Without the core, the Core-Skull absorbs the player's shadow energy and gains 20% health every 5 seconds).

The player's weapon, 'shard of the void', is weak against the Flicker-Swarm's bioluminescent phase. However, the shard emits a faint resonance when held—when the player activates it (via a prior encounter), it disrupts their phase shifts and causes them to stutter for 2 seconds. This is the *only* way to defeat them.

The Grief-Phantom attacks in silence, manifesting as a shadowy figure made of fragmented memories. It cannot be hurt directly. However, the Grief-Phantom is vulnerable to psychological dissonance—exposure to the Resonance Fragment's harmonic pulse (activated from the prior encounter) causes it to momentarily freeze, reducing its damage output by 50% for 3 seconds. This gives the player a chance to strike.

The Warden of Absence is a sentient construct built from the station's lost data and failed experiments. It has no physical form and manifests in digital projections. It can phase through walls. However, it is vulnerable to the 'Echo of the First Burn' pickup. When the player uses the memory echo to project a past event (specifically the moment when the Flicker-Swarm first appeared), the Warden destabilizes and becomes vulnerable. The player must *replay* that event (by using the memory echo to activate it), causing the Warden to freeze for 4 seconds—during which the player can deal 50% damage above normal.
Player uses Sparkler Whip to create a whistle (flick twice). The whistle stops its bounce and causes a ripple of sound that triggers the next encounter.
The player must use the Sparkler Whip's 'whistle' on the Disco Ball. When the whistle hits it, it freezes and shatters.
Use the Wobble Key on it. When used, the clock freezes and says 'Time is fixed!'
Tectonic Core Pulse (direct pulse over 8 seconds with 100% charge, targeting the core node at the center of its bloom pattern).

The player's own Tectonic Core Pulse used in reverse (called 'Reverse Pulse')—must be delivered within 2 seconds of enemy's gravity spike. Reverse Pulse disables its structural integrity for 5 seconds. Cannot be used if the Gravity Lens has not been acquired from the first encounter.

The Gravity Lens must be placed at a specific 45° rotational angle within 3 seconds of the core's central pulse (emitted every 90 seconds). When placed, it emits a pulse that disrupts the lattice's energy field for 10 seconds. The core will collapse if the lens is not placed during its active phase or if the player fails to align it properly.
